THE SHANGHAI TIMES, TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 22, 1931.

Why Pick And Levitsky Got
Year's Imprisonment

Written Judgment Is Delivered By First District
Court Setting Out Reasons For Conviction
Of Foreigners In Famous Arms Case

A written judgment has been delivered by the First District Court giving reasons for the conviction of Eugene Pick and Maurice Levitsky on charges of posing as military advisers to the Chinese Army in an arms deal involving $1,800,000. Both accused were sentenced to a year's imprisonment each after a lengthy trial. Wei Siau-lai, a Chinese accomplice, was sentenced to two months' imprisonment for aiding and abetting the other accused in an attempt to extort $69,000 from one Sze Tsoh-zung.

The Judgment

The full text of the judgment, translated into English from the Chinese, follows:—

Reasons.—(1) Re: Charge of False Representation. The accused Levitsky and Pick represented themselves as military advisers to the National Government. Both Raphael and Carroll have testified to this effect. Even Ralf, who introduced Pick in the transaction, stated: "When Pick came to see me he told me that he was a military adviser to the National Government." On June 17 Pick stated in court: "Raphael bought firearms for the Canton Government, and as we were military advisers to the National Government, we tried to get evidence in order to lay an information." On July 4 he, however, stated: "When I said I was military adviser to the Chinese Government, I meant that four years ago I was under Tang Seng-chi in the capacity of an adviser." All these tend to prove the fact that the accused have falsely represented themselves to be military advisers. The Government appoints advisers in order to get advice on Government affairs, and they are, therefore, engaged for discharge of public functions according to law. As the accused openly without authority make use of such official title, they should be dealt with according to Art. 166 of the Criminal Code. Wei Siau-lai admitted being a private secretary to Chang Fah-ying. As this is different from making use of an official title without authority, he should not be found guilty of the same offence.

Gas Masks and Barbed Wires
(2) Re: Charge of Attempted Extortion. Levitsky and Pick in the name of Chang Fah-ying made an agreement with Raphael. Raphael and the accused have produced such agreement for examination. Levitsky contended that such agreement was made between Raphael and Chang Fah-ying and that as he was employed in his firm, he retained it when he saw same. He denied having concluded any agreement in his name. Upon being cross-examined in this Court, Wei Siau-lai stated: "Tsigaraly introduced me to Levitsky and Pick. On the 24th, I went with Levitsky to see Raphael. He introduced me as Chang Fah-ying's secretary. I heard them talk about the purchase of pistols and rifles, but not the gas masks and barbed wires. It was said that the Canton Government wanted to buy these things and that the goods were to be delivered at Canton. Levitsky came out and told me that the guarantor must be Tsu Ts-yau and that as soon as Tsu agreed to it he would engage a Chinese lawyer and open negotiations with him. He also said that as they bought firearms for the Canton Government and Tsu Ts-yau acted as guarantor, it would be possible for him to extort money from them. Levitsky and Pick also spoke about the share they would get out of the profit. I told them I would not get any commission. I went twice altogether." Such a statement made by a joint accused unfavourable to himself describing vividly how they planned and attempted to extort money, should be accepted and based upon to prove the facts of the case. Sze Tseh-zung stated: "On the 13th Levitsky came to ask me to demand $69,000 commission from Raphael and the parties concerned. I went first to Tsu Ts-yau's place telling him that Canton was in rebellion and that as the arms were bought added after the agreement had been typed. However, the typist of Raphael and Co., stated that he typed part of the agreement and that the amount, place of delivery and date were all left blank. Thus it seems that a number of words were added in the agreement later and, therefore, it is difficult to conclude that the words "guaranteed by" were added by the accused. Furthermore, on June 9 Raphael wrote to Chang Fah-ying stating: "I am sure the agreement can be signed to-morrow. Nicholas Tau (Tsu Ts-yau) and P. Heath and Co., shall officially sign as witnesses and guarantors." Thus when Tau Ts-yau signed on the 10th he not only agreed to be witness but also agreed to accept responsibility as guarantor. Therefore, the words "guaranteed by" in the agreement cannot be regarded as forged.

(3) Re: Charge of Forging Bill and Chop. Levitsky went to the Mei Tai Printing Shop to have a chop made bearing Raphael's name. He went to get the chop on the 16th and stamped it on the bill which he carried with him. He also borrowed the "duplicate" chop from Mei Tai and stamped it on the top of the bill. He paid for the chop and then left it there. He was soon arrested outside of the shop by detectives and found in his possession were the bill, the draft copy of the bill and receipt for what he paid for the chop. Woo Tse-ziang, manager of the Mei Tai Printing Shop, D. S. I. Bebenin and D. S. Harvey all testified in court to the above effect and the bills, receipt, etc., were produced in court for examination. Accused admitted his own handwriting in the draft copy of the bill but contended that he only made a copy of it. However, in the draft a number of corrections were found. We can, therefore, conclude that it was a draft, not a copy accused had made and that accused should accept responsibility for forging the chop and documents.

In view of the reasons mentioned above, Levitsky should be dealt with according to Art. 42, 370 sec. 1 and 3, 39, 74, 166, 224, 234 sec. 1 and 70 sec. 3 of the Criminal Code; Pick should be dealt with according to Art. 42, 370 sec. 1 and 3, 39, 66 sec. 2 of the Criminal Code; and Wei Siau-lai for aiding and abetting shall receive the punishment prescribed for the offence reduced by one-half according to Art. 44, sec. 3, 370 sec. 1 and 3 and 39 of the Criminal Code.

JUDGE HYUI KYA-SHIH.
August 29, 1931.

《字林西报》，1931年9月22日，星期二。

为何皮克（Pick）与列维茨基（Levitsky）获判一年监禁

第一特区法院作出书面判决，阐述在著名军火案中对两名外国人定罪的理由

第一特区法院已就尤金·皮克（Eugene Pick）和莫里斯·列维茨基（Maurice Levitsky）在一宗涉及180万美元的军火交易中冒充中国军队军事顾问的指控作出书面判决，并阐述了定罪理由。经过漫长的审判，两名被告均被判处一年监禁。中国同谋魏小来（Wei Siau-lai，音译）因协助并教唆其他被告企图向施作忠（Sze Tsoh-zung，音译）勒索69,000美元，被判处两个月监禁。

判决书

判决书全文由中文译为英文，如下：—

理由.—(1) 关于虚假陈述罪。被告列维茨基和皮克自称是国民政府的军事顾问。拉斐尔（Raphael）和卡罗尔（Carroll）均就此作证。甚至介绍皮克参与交易的拉尔夫（Ralf）也 stated：“当皮克来见我时，他告诉我他是国民政府的军事顾问。”6月17日，皮克在法庭上称：“拉斐尔为广东政府购买枪支，由于我们是国民政府的军事顾问，我们试图获取证据以便提出控告。”然而，7月4日他却称：“我说我是中国政府的军事顾问，意思是我四年前曾在唐生智手下担任顾问。”所有这些均倾向于证明被告虚假自称军事顾问的事实。政府任命顾问是为了就政府事务征求意见，因此他们是依法受聘履行公共职能。由于被告公开且未经授权地使用此类官方头衔，应根据《刑法》第166条予以处理。魏小来承认自己是张发英（Chang Fah-ying，音译）的私人秘书。这与未经授权冒用官方头衔不同，故不应认定其犯有同一罪行。

防毒面具与铁丝网
(2) 关于企图勒索罪。列维茨基和皮克以张发英的名义与拉斐尔达成协议。拉斐尔和被告已提交该协议以供审查。列维茨基辩称，该协议是拉斐尔与张发英之间签订的，由于他受雇于该公司，他在看到协议时将其保留。他否认以自己名义签订任何协议。在本庭接受交叉讯问时，魏小来陈述：“齐加拉利（Tsigaraly，音译）将我介绍给列维茨基和皮克。24日，我随列维茨基去见拉斐尔。他将我介绍为张发英的秘书。我听到他们谈论购买手枪和步枪，但未提及防毒面具和铁丝网。据说广东政府想购买这些物品，货物将在广东交付。列维茨基出来说，担保人必须是徐子耀（Tsu Ts-yau，音译），一旦徐同意，他就会聘请一名中国律师并与之展开谈判。他还说，由于他们为广东政府购买枪支，且徐子耀担任担保人，他有可能向他们勒索钱财。列维茨基和皮克还谈论了他们将从利润中获得的份额。我告诉他们我不会收取任何佣金。我总共去了两次。”共同被告作出的这一不利于己的陈述，生动描述了他们策划并企图勒索钱财的过程，应予采信并作为认定案件事实的依据。施泽宗（Sze Tseh-zung，音译）陈述：“13日，列维茨基来找我，要求我向拉斐尔及相关方索要69,000美元佣金。我先去了徐子耀处，告诉他广东正在叛乱，且武器是在协议打字完成后追加购买的。然而，拉斐尔公司的打字员陈述，他打印了部分协议，金额、交货地点和日期均留空。因此，似乎协议后来添加了一些词语，因此难以断定“由……担保”字样是由被告添加的。此外，6月9日拉斐尔致信张发英称：“我确信协议明天可以签署。尼古拉斯·陶（Nicholas Tau，即徐子耀）和P. Heath公司将正式作为见证人和担保人签字。”因此，当陶子耀（Tau Ts-yau，即徐子耀）于10日签字时，他不仅同意作为见证人，还同意承担担保人责任。因此，协议中的“由……担保”字样不能被视为伪造。

(3) 关于伪造票据和印章罪。列维茨基前往美泰印刷店（Mei Tai Printing Shop）刻制一枚带有拉斐尔姓名的印章。他于16日去取印章，并将其盖在他随身携带的票据上。他还从美泰借用了“副本”印章，盖在票据顶部。他支付了印章费用后将印章留在那里。他很快在店外被侦探逮捕，在其身上发现了票据、票据草稿以及支付印章费用的收据。美泰印刷店经理吴子江（Woo Tse-ziang，音译）、侦探副督察贝贝宁（D. S. I. Bebenin）和侦探哈维（D. S. Harvey）均在法庭上就上述情况作证，票据、收据等物证已提交法庭审查。被告承认票据草稿上的笔迹为其本人所写，但辩称那只是抄本。然而，在草稿中发现了多处修改。因此，我们可以得出结论，那是草稿而非被告制作的抄本，被告应承担伪造印章和文件的责任。

鉴于上述理由，列维茨基应根据《刑法》第42条、第370条第1款和第3款、第39条、第74条、第166条、第224条、第234条第1款及第70条第3款予以处理；皮克应根据《刑法》第42条、第370条第1款和第3款、第39条、第66条第2款予以处理；魏小来因协助和教唆，应根据《刑法》第44条第3款、第370条第1款和第3款及第39条规定，按该罪行应受处罚减半论处。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES. TUESDAY, AUGUST 25, 1931

THE PICK CASE
Editor
THE SHANGHAI TIMES
Sir,—I read the following in the local papers which have related the 'Pick Case':
"Upon the opening of court yesterday, Pick announced that he had dismissed Mr. Paul Premet as one of his counsel and charged that the attorney refused to return to him certain document necessary to his defence unless the sum of $170 was paid on account of interpretation and balance of fees."
I give you below the text of the letter I received from Pick a few hours before the last hearing:
"Amoy Gaol, August 20, 1931, 2 p.m.
Mr. Paul Premet,
"I have decided to have no lawyer; therefore send to the court at 9 a.m.: (1) my file, (2) photos, etc. . . .
"I give up your assistance not because I do not trust you, but I consider it will be better for me and worse for Raphael.
"(Signed) KLIGE PICK.
"P. S. at the same time I renounce to attorney Franklin Chu."
From that letter, every one see that Pick did not charge me at all that I refused to return some documents on account fees being unpaid.
The truth is, that Pick thought at the last hour that it should be better not to be defended: Perhaps he is true.
PAUL PREMET.
Shanghai, Aug. 24, 1931.

《字林西报》
先生，——我在本地报纸上读到有关“皮克案”的如下报道：
“昨日开庭时，皮克宣布已解聘保罗·普雷梅（Paul Premet）先生为其辩护律师之一，并指控该律师拒绝向他归还对其辩护至关重要的某些文件，除非支付170美元作为翻译费及部分未结律师费。”
现将我在最后一次听证会前几小时收到皮克来信的全文刊登如下：
“厦门监狱，1931年8月20日，下午2时。
保罗·普雷梅先生：
我已决定不聘请律师；因此请于上午9时向法院提交：(1) 我的案卷，(2) 照片等……
“我放弃您的协助并非因为我不信任您，而是我认为这对我更有利，而对拉斐尔（Raphael）更不利。
“（签名）克利格·皮克（KLIGE PICK）。
“附言：同时我也放弃朱富兰克林（Franklin Chu）律师的服务。”
从该信可以看出，皮克根本没有指控我因费用未付而拒绝归还某些文件。
事实是，皮克在最后一刻认为不进行辩护或许更好：也许他是对的。
保罗·普雷梅。

Third Accused Testifies In Arms Dealing Trial
Chinese Gives Evidence Against Pick And Levitsky,
Another Charge Of Attempted Extortion Is Added To List

The trial of Eugene Pick and Levitsky before Judge Hyui in the Shanghai Special District Court yesterday was featured by the evidence of Wei Siau-lai, third accused and associate of his companions in the dock, who testified against them. After several witnesses were called the case was adjourned for a week.

Pick and Levitsky who were originally charged with false representation and counterfeiting a chop of Mr. R. K. Raphael, complainant in the case, yesterday were further charged with attempting to extort money from Mr. Nicholas Hsu, a witness. Wei was charged with aiding Pick and Levitsky in the alleged attempted extortion. He was defended by Mr. Y. T. Van while Mr. Franklin Chio appeared for Levitsky, Mr. Paul Premec for Pick and Mr. Paul Y. Ru, Assistant Municipal Advocate prosecuted.

The prosecution arose from an alleged deal in arms involving $180,000. It was alleged that Pick and Levitsky posed as representatives of the purchasing department of the Chinese military authorities who, they said, wanted to buy the arms which were to be supplied by Mr. Raphael.

Pick previously told the Court that he had reported to Mr. T. V. Soong, Minister of Finance, regarding an arms deal with the Canton clique and that he was referred to the Superintendent of Customs.

At the outset yesterday Judge Hyui said he had received a reply to his letter from the Customs stating that Pick had reported to them that a deal in arms was going on in the office of Mr. Raphael. The reply further stated that the Customs did not authorize Pick to make any inquiries about the matter.

The Chinese accused was then called. He made the following statement: When he met the other two accused he was told that they were going to carry on certain dealings with Chinese. Both prisoners visited him at his home. Levitsky introduced him to Mr. Raphael as Levitsky's secretary. While in the office of Mr. Raphael he overheard certain negotiations regarding arms and ammunition. Mention was made of a number of rifles and Mauser pistols. The prices were discussed. He gathered that the shipment of arms was destined for Canton.

Continuing, accused said that on his second visit to the office of Mr. Raphael the topic of conversation included General Chan Fah-ying, a brother of General Chan Fah-kwei. The conversation took place in the presence of Mr. Carroll. He told Levitsky, with whom he left the office, that he was reluctant to take any part in the dealings. He was later told by Pick that he would benefit as there would be dinners with plenty of food and champagne.

Guarantor Wanted

Witness went on to say that he was told by the other prisoners that they would go to a lawyer to make Mr. Nicholas Hsu pay their commission for the arms deal, after the contract was signed. Mr. Hsu was alleged to be a witness to the contract.

Reverting to his second visit to the office of Mr. Raphael, witness said his companions in the dock asked Mr. Raphael to get a guarantor of the contract and Mr. Raphael replied that he had many Chinese friends from whom Nicholas Hsu was subsequently chosen. He heard Levitsky remark to Mr. Raphael that the first thing to do would be to get the guarantors, failing which witnesses to the contract would have to be secured. He did not hear that General Chan Fah-ying would not sign the contract if there were no guarantors. The other accused told him they would be witnesses to the contract and asked him to print cards for General Chan Fah-ying. He said they also told him that he was too young to pose as the general, and that an older man would be required. He could not say who subsequently masqueraded as General Chan Fah-ying.

Witness declared that he did not represent himself as an officer and was not promised any remuneration. Mr. Raphael, recalled, said that Pick and Levitsky and other crooks went to his office to try to take advantage of him and his friend.

第三名被告在军火交易审判中作证
华人对皮克（Pick）和列维茨基（Levitsky）提供不利证词，
企图勒索的另一项指控被加入起诉名单

昨日，在上海特区法院，由许慧（Hyui）法官主持审理尤金·皮克（Eugene Pick）和列维茨基（Levitsky）一案，庭审的焦点是第三名被告魏小来（Wei Siau-lai，音译）提供的证词，他是被告席上其同伙的伙伴，并对他们提供了不利证词。在传唤了几名证人后，案件休庭一周。

皮克和列维茨基最初被控虚假陈述及伪造本案原告 R. K. 拉斐尔（R. K. Raphael）先生的印章，昨日又被加控企图向证人尼古拉斯·许（Nicholas Hsu）先生勒索钱财。魏被控协助皮克和列维茨基进行所谓的企图勒索。魏由范永泰（Y. T. Van，音译）律师辩护，富兰克林·乔（Franklin Chio，音译）律师代表列维茨基出庭，保罗·普雷梅克（Paul Premec，音译）律师代表皮克出庭，助理市检察官鲁保罗（Paul Y. Ru，音译）提起公诉。

本案源于一宗据称涉及18万美元的军火交易。据称，皮克和列维茨基冒充中国军事当局采购部门的代表，声称该部门希望购买由拉斐尔先生供应的军火。

皮克此前曾告诉法庭，他就与广东派系的一笔军火交易向财政部长宋子文（T. V. Soong）先生作了汇报，随后被引荐给海关税务司。

昨日庭审开始时，许慧法官表示，他已收到海关对其去信的回复，称皮克曾向他们报告说，拉斐尔先生的办公室内正在进行一笔军火交易。回复还指出，海关并未授权皮克就此事进行任何调查。

随后传召了这名华人被告。他作了如下陈述：当他遇到另外两名被告时，被告知他们将与中国方面进行某些交易。两名囚犯都曾到他的家中拜访。列维茨基将他作为列维茨基的秘书介绍给拉斐尔先生。在拉斐尔先生的办公室里，他无意中听到了一些关于军火和弹药的谈判。提到了若干支步枪和毛瑟手枪。双方讨论了价格。他得知这批军火的目的地是广州。

被告继续说道，在他第二次访问拉斐尔先生的办公室时，谈话内容包括陈济棠将军的兄弟陈维周（Chan Fah-ying，音译）将军。谈话是在卡罗尔（Carroll）先生在场的情况下进行的。他与列维茨基离开办公室时，告诉列维茨基他不愿参与这些交易。后来皮克告诉他，他将从中受益，因为会有丰盛的晚宴和香槟。

需要担保人

证人接着说，其他囚犯告诉他，在合同签署后，他们会去找一名律师，迫使尼古拉斯·许先生支付他们在军火交易中的佣金。据称许先生是该合同的见证人。

回到他第二次访问拉斐尔先生办公室的话题，证人说，被告席上的同伴要求拉斐尔先生为合同寻找一名担保人，拉斐尔先生回答说他有许多中国朋友，随后从中选中了尼古拉斯·许。他听到列维茨基对拉斐尔先生说，首先要做的是获得担保人，否则就必须确保有合同见证人。他没有听到如果没有担保人，陈维周将军就不会签署合同的说法。其他被告告诉他，他们将担任合同的见证人，并要求他为陈维周将军印制名片。他说他们还告诉他，他太年轻，不适合冒充这位将军，需要一位年长的人。他说不出后来是谁冒充了陈维周将军。

证人声明，他并未自称是军官，也没有人承诺给他任何报酬。被再次传唤的拉斐尔先生说，皮克、列维茨基和其他骗子去他的办公室，试图利用他和他的朋友。

（手写批注：嘿，请归档。M.G. 31.8.17.）

法官询问尼古拉斯·许（Nicholas Hsu）先生进行过多少次军火交易，他回答说，是匹克公司（P. Heath and Company）请他作为军火合同的见证人签字。

证人接着叙述，在一个星期六的晚上，皮克（Pick）和列维茨基（Levitsky）带着一名律师来到他家，要求每支步枪抽取9美元的佣金，并威胁他说，这是一笔危险的交易，作为拉斐尔（Raphael）先生的担保人，如果他们无法从拉斐尔先生那里拿到佣金，就得向他追讨。随后，他们要求他请求拉斐尔先生支付佣金，称他作为担保人负有责任。他回答说，他以为这笔交易是与南京方面进行的，这时他们指出合同上提到了广州。对此，他们告诉他，由于交易对象是广州，他无法推卸责任。

中国律师施先生（Mr. Sze）随后陈述，列维茨基授予他代理权，向拉斐尔先生收取69,000美元的佣金。他说，列维茨基告诉他，交易已经完成，相关款项也已支付。证人表示，他原以为交易是与南京方面进行的，在审阅合同副本时发现其中提到广州，感到十分惊讶。他说，应列维茨基先生的要求，他也去见了尼古拉斯·许先生。当保罗·普雷梅特（Paul Premet）先生问他去见尼古拉斯·许先生是受其当事人建议还是出于主动时，证人回答他是奉命前往。

列维茨基随后陈述，他是在拉斐尔先生的办公室被介绍给中国被告的，并请上一位证人通过拜访许先生来核实合同上尼古拉斯·许先生的签名。他否认曾与律师一同去“向许先生索取佣金”。他声称，这名中国被告正在协助拉斐尔先生向绑匪和共产党人供应军火。

再次提及防毒面具

尽管拉斐尔先生否认出售过防毒面具，但列维茨基继续说道，保罗·普雷梅特先生手中的文件将证明事实并非如此。普雷梅特先生随即出示了一个防毒面具，并承认他持有列维茨基所提到的文件。

接下来传唤的一位俄罗斯证人说，在列维茨基向他寻求一名翻译后，他将中国被告介绍给了列维茨基。后来中国人告诉他，他不会与列维茨基做生意，因此也不会再去拜访列维茨基。

ARRESTED AS ACCOMPLICE

Chinese in Court in Connection with Charges Against Pick, Levitsky

With reference to the case in which Eugene Pick and M. Levitsky were charged in the Shanghai Special District Court with falsely representing themselves as the military advisers to the Nanking Government and with forging a seal and fraudulently using the same on a contract in a manner likely to cause injury to the complainant R. K. Raphael, the Municipal Police arrested, on Wednesday morning, an important Chinese witness in the case named Wei Shao-lan, residing at No. 33 Min Teh Lee Alleyway, off Rue Bourgeat, French Concession.

The arrested man was arraigned before Judge Hyui, who had tried Pick and Levitsky, yesterday morning on a charge of being concerned with Pick and Levitsky in attempting to defraud the complainant R. K. Raphael of over $1,000,000 worth of arms. Accused made some startling statements and alleged that the real intention of Pick and Levitsky was not to defraud R. K. Raphael, but to extort a huge sum of money from some rich Chinese who agreed to act as guarantors for the complainant and who attached their signatures to the contract whereby the arms supposed to have been ordered from abroad would be shipped to the rebel leaders in Canton.

With Other Accused
Mr. Paul Y. Ru, Assistant Municipal Advocate, prosecuting, told the Court that, when Pick and Levitsky visited the complainant firm to "negotiate" regarding the purchase of over $1,000,000 worth of arms, they were accompanied by accused who was introduced to the complainant by Levitsky and described as the secretary to Gen. Chang Fa-ying who Pick and Levitsky stated was a younger brother of Gen. Chang Fa-kuei and represented the Chinese Government. After the arrest of Pick and Levitsky, counsel stated, the police conducted extensive inquiries regarding accused's whereabouts in order to bring him to book for trial with the two other accused. However, efforts made by the police to locate accused failed until 9 a.m. on Wednesday when Sub.-Inspr. Bebenin accompanied by a Chinese detective, acting upon information received, proceeded to the French Concession and arrested accused in his house at No. 33 Min Teh Lee Alleyway, off Rue Bourgeat.

Complainant corroborated and stated that accused had, together with Pick and Levitsky, visited his office four or five times, his first visit to his office being on May 24. At first, complainant said, he did not suspect accused as being concerned with the two other accused in attempting to defraud him as he was well-dressed and looked like a well-to-do Chinese. Subsequently, when Pick and Levitsky were arrested by the police, he gave to the police information concerning accused's description and this had led to accused's arrest.

Questioned by the Court, accused vigorously denied the charge and made a lengthy statement regarding his connection with Pick and Levitsky. He said he was formerly employed by the Tientsin-Pukow Railway when he became acquainted with a Russian named Tsikareli who also worked on the railway. Subsequently, he and Tsikareli lost their jobs and came to Shanghai.

Acts as Interpreter

On May 24, accused said, Tsikareli visited his house in the French Concession and asked him to act as an interpreter between certain foreigners and Chinese in arranging a business transaction. Being jobless and badly in need of money, he agreed and then Tsikareli took him to No. 24 Rue des Soeurs where he was introduced first to Levitsky and then to Pick. The latter took him to the complainant's office in Canton Road and, whilst there, he "heard" that Levitsky introduced him to the complainant and described him as the secretary to Gen. Chang Fa-ying.

"I never introduced myself to the complainant and described myself as a secretary to Gen. Chang Fa-ying as alleged by the police and, if the Court does not believe me, the complainant, Mr. Raphael will testify to this effect," accused told the Court.

Continuing, accused stated that, when he heard that he was being described by Levitsky as a secretary to Gen. Chang Fa-ying, he was greatly surprised as he had never held such a job before, so he remained silent all the time when negotiations regarding the purchase of arms were going on between Pick and the complainant. When they left the complainant firm, he refused to go there again, but, several days later, Pick and Levitsky called at him and asked him to visit the complainant firm once more. He refused, but Pick and Levitsky called at his house again and again until he finally consented. However, he paid only two visits to the complainant firm and not four or five visits as alleged by the complainant. Accused denied having any knowledge of the signing of the contract between Pick and the complainant or of the forging of the complainant's seal by Levitsky.

Allegation of Blackmail

In conclusion, accused alleged that the real intention of Pick and Levitsky in entering into a contract with the complainant regarding the purchase of over $1,000,000 worth of arms was not to defraud the complainant who was a foreigner and who was not a man whom one could easily defraud. The real intention of Pick and Levitsky was, accused alleged, to get some wealthy Chinese to act as guarantors for the complainant in the arms transaction and, when the wealthy Chinese attached their signatures to the contract whereby the arms supposed to have been ordered from abroad would be shipped to the rebel leaders in Canton, they would extract a huge sum of money from the Chinese by threatening to report to Gen. Chiang Kai-shek on the contents of the contract. The Chinese, being afraid of being arrested by their Government, would give in and settle the matter in whatever way Pick and Levitsky desired.

On account of this, accused stated, Pick and Levitsky, during their negotiations with the complainant, insisted that the latter should find one or two leading Chinese merchants to act as his guarantors. At first, accused alleged, the complainant suggested that he should invite Mr. Koo Shing-yi, a leading merchant of Nantao and a member of the Chinese Chamber of Commerce, to act as his guarantor, but to this Pick disagreed. The complainant then suggested Mr. Nichola Chu, to which Pick agreed, so Mr. Chu's name appeared on the contract. Accused further stated that Pick had promised him a sum of money if their scheme was successfully carried into effect.

Sub.-Inspr. Bebenin having given his evidence of arrest, the Court remanded the case sine die, accused being ordered to be kept in custody, pending his trial with Pick and Levitsky.

作为共犯被捕

华人因涉及对皮克、列维茨基的指控出庭受审

关于尤金·皮克（Eugene Pick）和M.列维茨基（M. Levitsky）在上海特区法院被控虚假自称是南京政府的军事顾问，并在一份合同中伪造印章并以可能对原告R. K.拉斐尔（R. K. Raphael）造成损害的方式欺诈性使用该印章一案，工部局警务处于周三上午逮捕了该案的一名重要华人证人，名为魏少兰（Wei Shao-lan，音译），住址为法租界布尔热路（Rue Bourgeat）旁明德里33号。

被捕男子于昨日上午在审理皮克和列维茨基案件的许伊法官（Judge Hyui，音译）面前受审，被控与皮克和列维茨基合谋，企图诈骗原告R. K.拉斐尔价值超过100万美元的军火。被告做出了一些惊人的陈述，并声称皮克和列维茨基的真正意图并非诈骗R. K.拉斐尔，而是向一些同意担任原告担保人并在合同上签名的富有华人勒索巨额钱财，该合同规定所谓从国外订购的军火将运往广州的反叛领袖处。

与其他被告一起

助理市政检察官保罗·鲁（Paul Y. Ru）先生在起诉时告诉法庭，当皮克和列维茨基访问原告商号“洽谈”购买价值超过100万美元的军火时，由被告陪同，被告由列维茨基介绍给原告，并被描述为张发英将军（Gen. Chang Fa-ying，音译）的秘书；皮克和列维茨基称张发英是张发奎将军（Gen. Chang Fa-kuei）的弟弟，代表中国政府。检察官称，在皮克和列维茨基被捕后，警方就被告的下落进行了广泛调查，以便将其缉拿归案，与另外两名被告一同受审。然而，警方 locating 被告的努力一直失败，直到周三上午9点，副督察贝贝宁（Sub.-Inspr. Bebenin）在一名华探的陪同下，根据获得的情报，前往法租界，在布尔热路旁明德里33号的家中逮捕了被告。

原告予以佐证并陈述，被告曾与皮克和列维茨基一起访问他的办公室四五次，首次访问是在5月24日。原告说，起初他并未怀疑被告与另外两名被告合谋诈骗他，因为被告衣着考究，看起来像是一位富裕的华人。后来，当皮克和列维茨基被警方逮捕时，他向警方提供了有关被告体貌特征的信息，这导致了被告的被捕。

经法庭讯问，被告坚决否认指控，并就其与皮克和列维茨基的关系作了长篇陈述。他说，他以前在津浦铁路任职时，结识了一位也在该铁路工作的名叫齐卡雷利（Tsikareli，音译）的俄罗斯人。后来，他和齐卡雷利都失去了工作，来到了上海。

担任翻译

被告说，5月24日，齐卡雷利来到他在法租界的家中，请他在某些外国人与华人安排一笔商业交易时担任翻译。由于失业且急需用钱，他同意了，随后齐卡雷利带他去了修女路（Rue des Soeurs）24号，在那里他先被介绍给列维茨基，然后介绍给皮克。后者带他去了广东路原告的办公室，在那里，他“听到”列维茨基将他介绍给原告，并称他为张发英将军的秘书。

“我从未像警方指控的那样向原告自我介绍并自称是张发英将军的秘书，如果法庭不相信我，原告拉斐尔先生可以为此作证，”被告告诉法庭。

被告继续陈述，当他听到列维茨基将他描述为张发英将军的秘书时，他感到非常惊讶，因为他以前从未担任过这样的职务，所以在皮克与原告进行军火采购谈判期间，他一直保持沉默。当他们离开原告商号时，他拒绝再去那里，但几天后，皮克和列维茨基来找他，请他再次访问原告商号。他拒绝了，但皮克和列维茨基一次又一次地到他家里拜访，直到他最终同意。然而，他只去过原告商号两次，而不是原告所称的四五次。被告否认知晓皮克与原告之间合同的签署，或列维茨基伪造原告印章一事。

敲诈勒索的指控

最后，被告声称，皮克和列维茨基与原告签订关于购买价值超过100万美元军火的合同的真正意图，并非诈骗原告这位外国人，因为原告不是一个容易被诈骗的人。被告声称，皮克和列维茨基的真正意图是让一些富有的华人在军火交易中担任原告的担保人，当这些富有的华人在合同上签名，规定所谓从国外订购的军火将运往广州的反叛领袖处时，他们便以向蒋介石将军报告合同内容相威胁，向华人勒索巨额钱财。华人因害怕被本国政府逮捕，便会屈服，并按皮克和列维茨基希望的任何方式解决此事。

被告称，因此，皮克和列维茨基在与原告谈判期间，坚持要求原告找一两位华商领袖担任其担保人。被告声称，起初原告建议邀请南市著名商人、中国商会会员顾星一（Koo Shing-yi，音译）先生担任其担保人，但皮克不同意。原告随后建议朱尼科拉（Nichola Chu，音译）先生，皮克同意了，因此朱先生的名字出现在合同上。被告进一步陈述，皮克曾承诺，如果他们的计划成功实施，将给他一笔钱。

副督察贝贝宁提供逮捕证词后，法庭宣布本案无限期延期审理，被告被命令收押候审，等待与皮克和列维茨基一同受审。

THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES, JULY 26, 1931

Double Forgery Suggested
In Arms Deal Trial

Levitsky Denies Having Ordered Counterfeit Chop
Of British Complainant; Declares He Was Agent
Of Mr. Raphael; Hearing Adjourned

A declaration that there had been a double forgery was made by Mr. R. K. Raphael, British complainant, at the adjourned hearing before Judge Hyui in the Shanghai Special District Court yesterday of the prosecution against Eugene Pick and Levitsky. Accused were again remanded indefinitely on charges of posing as representatives of the Chinese military authorities. Levitsky faces the additional charge of making a counterfeit chop. Prisoners were arrested following a deal in arms involving more than $1,000,000.

Mr. Paul Y. Ru, Assistant Municipal Advocate, prosecuting, said the police would produce three detectives to give evidence in connection with the second charge against Levitsky.

Wu Tse-hsiang, proprietor of the Mei Tah Printing shop where the forged chop of Mr. Raphael was claimed to have been made was called first. He related how Levitsky visited his establishment and ordered a chop for delivery the same day. As the chop was for the hong of Mr. Raphael his suspicions were aroused and he informed Mr. Raphael.

Accused's Denial

Levitsky pointed out that the Mei Tah Printing shop supplied all the stationery of Mr. Raphael. It was inconceivable he said, that he should go to them to make a forged chop of Mr. Raphael.

Levitsky went on to say that he saw the proprietor of the Mei Tah Printing shop in the office of Mr. Raphael in several occasions. The last time he saw the printer there he had ordered some visiting cards with his name as agent for R. K. Raphael and Company underneath. Continuing, he said, this was done with the consent of Mr. Raphael, and that it had been arranged for him to go to Dairen to look after a shipment for Mr. Raphael.

On the day of his arrest Levitsky said, he met Mr. Raphael on the street and they spoke about a contract for the supply of arms. Mr. Raphael he said, remarked to him: "We are all in China to make money." He then promised to take the contract the next day to the office of Mr. Raphael who he said told him to go the printer and get his cards. He called at the Mei Tah printing shop, but the owner was out and he was told that the cards were locked up in a drawer and that he could return that afternoon for them.

Copied Specification

Before leaving the shop Levitsky said, he saw a specification of a table and was told that Mr. Raphael had ordered 100 of it to be printed. Upon noticing that the specification related to arms he made a copy of the specification of a piece of paper for future reference.

On returning to the shop in the afternoon Levitsky continued he met the proprietor who told him that his cards had been sent to Mr. Raphael. The proprietor he said, also told him that he could take the specification he had seen in the morning to Mr. Raphael and inform Mr. Raphael that the 100 forms would be finished the following day. The speaker, he said, then folded the specification and gave it to him. After putting it in his pocket he took out his copy of it and tore it up. The printer he said, also gave him the stamp with the name of Mr. Raphael's hong and told him that Mr. Raphael had ordered it. He replied that he was not going again to see Mr. Raphael that day and asked the printer to take the chop himself.

Levitsky then denied that he had ordered the chop and pointed out that it was not found on him at the time of his arrest and declared that it would be ridiculous for him to order it from the printer of Mr. Raphael.

Police Witness

The first police witness called was Detective Sub-Inspector V. C. Bebenin of Central Station. After receiving a report on June 16 he said, he went in the afternoon with Detective Sergeant Harvie and a Chinese detective to the Mei Tah printing shop. They were told by the proprietor that a foreigner who ordered the chop would return at 4 p.m. for it. At that time they did not know who the foreigner was. They concealed themselves and at 4 p.m. were told that the foreigner had arrived. The other two detectives remained in the shop while he waited outside to prevent the foreigner from escaping. After a few minutes he saw Levitsky coming out. He immediately stopped and searched Levitsky and found a certain document in his pocket and small pieces of paper. By this time he was rejoined by the other detectives who told him that the foreigner had left the chop in the shop after making an impression of it on a document.

Military Equipment

After the other two detectives had given evidence Mr. Raphael was re-called. He said that Levitsky purchase of gas masks, military telephones etc. He wrote a letter from his home to General Chang Fah-ying assuring the recipient that he would get guarantors for the supply of arms if there was a proper endorsement from Nanking. The letter, witness declared, proved that the words 'Guaranteed by' on the contract must have been put in by one of the accused. The chop of Chang Fah-ying witness declared, was also a forgery. The words "Guaranteed by" and the stamp of Chang Fah-ying he said, were forged because after chopping the contract Chang must keep the letter as he was supposed to chop the contract on the strength of it. It was stated that Levitsky called at the home of Mr. Raphael in the evening for the letter which was never delivered to Chang Fah-ying.

Levitsky was then questioned by the Court and emphasized that the letter was handwritten and not typed as it should be in his opinion, if it was a document on the strength of which the contract would be signed. He admitted that General Chang Fah-ying had never seen the letter.

Further Adjournment

"Why should he want this letter?" Levitsky asked, "He has got the contract from Mr. Raphael for $2,000,000 worth of arms."

Before adjourning the proceedings Judge Hyui stated that no answer had been received from Mr. Tong the Superintendant of Customs, to the despatch sent by the Court since the last hearing. The despatch was in connection with a statement made by Pick that he had informed Mr. T. V. Soong, the Finance Minister, about the deal in arms and had handed certain documents relating to the deal to the Superintendant of Customs at the suggestion of the Minister. The judge said he would send another despatch to the Superintendant and adjourn the case indefinitely pending the receipt of a reply.

《上海星期时报》，1931年7月26日

军火交易审判中
暗示存在双重伪造

莱维茨基否认下令伪造英国控告人印章；声称其为拉斐尔先生代理人；听证会休庭

昨日，在上海特区法院惠伊（Hyui）法官主持下，针对尤金·皮克（Eugene Pick）和莱维茨基（Levitsky）的起诉案件在休庭后继续审理。英国控告人 R. K. 拉斐尔（R. K. Raphael）先生在庭上声明，此案涉及双重伪造。被告再次被无限期还押，罪名是冒充中国军事当局代表。莱维茨基还面临伪造印章的额外指控。囚犯是在一笔价值超过100万美元的军火交易之后被捕的。

助理市检察官保罗·Y·鲁（Paul Y. Ru）先生作为公诉方表示，警方将传唤三名侦探，就针对莱维茨基的第二项指控作证。

首先出庭的是美达（Mei Tah）印刷店的店主吴泽祥（Wu Tse-hsiang，音译），据称拉斐尔先生的伪造印章就是在此处制作的。他讲述了莱维茨基如何光顾他的店铺，并订购一枚当天交付的印章。由于该印章是用于拉斐尔先生的商号，这引起了他的怀疑，于是他通知了拉斐尔先生。

被告的否认

莱维茨基指出，美达印刷店供应拉斐尔先生的所有文具用品。他说，自己去那里制作拉斐尔先生的伪造印章是不可想象的。

莱维茨基接着说，他曾在拉斐尔先生的办公室里多次见过美达印刷店的店主。他最后一次在那里见到这位印刷商时，曾订购了一些名片，上面印有他的名字，下方注明为 R. K. 拉斐尔公司（R. K. Raphael and Company）的代理人。他继续说道，这是征得拉斐尔先生同意的，并且已安排他前往大连（Dairen）为拉斐尔先生照料一批货物。

莱维茨基说，在他被捕的那天，他在街上遇到了拉斐尔先生，他们谈论了一份军火供应合同。他说，拉斐尔先生对他 remarked（评论）道：“我们在中国都是为了赚钱。”随后，拉斐尔先生答应第二天把合同带到他的办公室，并告诉他去找印刷商取名片。他去了美达印刷店，但店主不在，有人告诉他名片锁在抽屉里，让他下午再来取。

复制规格单

莱维茨基说，在离开店铺之前，他看到一份表格的规格单，并得知拉斐尔先生已订购印制100份。当他注意到该规格单与军火有关时，他在一张纸上抄录了一份副本，以备日后参考。

莱维茨基继续说，下午回到店里时，他遇到了店主，店主告诉他名片已经送往拉斐尔先生处。他说，店主还告诉他，可以把早上看到的规格单拿给拉斐尔先生，并告知拉斐尔先生那100份表格将在第二天完成。他说，当时说话的人（指店主）将规格单折叠起来交给了他。他把规格单放进口袋后，拿出自己抄录的副本并将其撕毁。他说，印刷商还把刻有拉斐尔先生商号名称的印章交给了他，并告诉他这是拉斐尔先生订购的。他回答说那天他不再去见拉斐尔先生，并请印刷商自行送去印章。

莱维茨基随后否认是他订购了该印章，并指出在他被捕时印章并未在他身上搜出，他还宣称，向拉斐尔先生的印刷商订购印章是荒谬的。

警方证人

第一位出庭的警方证人是中央巡捕房的副巡官 V. C. Bebenin。他说，6月16日接到报告后，当天下午他与警长哈维（Harvie）及一名华探前往美达印刷店。店主告诉他们，订购印章的外国人将于下午4点回来取货。当时他们并不知道这名外国人是谁。他们藏身起来，下午4点时被告知该外国人已到。另外两名侦探留在店内，而他在外面守候，以防该外国人逃跑。几分钟后，他看见莱维茨基走出来。他立即上前拦截并搜查莱维茨基，在其口袋中发现了一份文件和一些小纸片。此时，另外两名侦探与他汇合，并告诉他那名外国人在一份文件上盖印后，将印章留在了店里。

军用装备

在另外两名侦探作证后，拉斐尔先生再次被传唤。他说，莱维茨基购买了防毒面具、军用电话等物品。他从家中写了一封信给张发英（Chang Fah-ying，音译）将军，向收信人保证，如果有南京方面的正式背书，他将获得军火供应的担保人。证人宣称，这封信证明合同上的“由……担保”（Guaranteed by）字样必定是由其中一名被告添加的。证人宣称，张发英的印章也是伪造的。他说，“由……担保”字样和张发英的印章之所以是伪造的，是因为在合同盖章后，张必须保留这封信，因为他理应是凭此信才在合同上盖章的。据称，莱维茨基当晚曾到拉斐尔先生家中索取这封信，但这封信从未送达张发英手中。

随后法庭对莱维茨基进行了讯问，他强调这封信是手写的，而不是打印的，他认为如果这是一份据以签署合同的正式文件，理应打印。他承认张发英将军从未见过这封信。

再次休庭

“他为什么要这封信？”莱维茨基问道，“他已经从拉斐尔先生那里拿到了价值200万美元的军火合同。”

在宣布休庭前，惠伊法官表示，自上次听证会以来，法院发给税务司唐先生（Mr. Tong）的公函未收到回复。该公函涉及皮克的一项陈述，即他曾向财政部长宋子文（T. V. Soong）通报过这笔军火交易，并根据部长的建议，将与交易有关的某些文件移交给了税务司。法官表示他将再发一封公函给税务司，并在收到回复前无限期休庭。

No. S. B. D. 2543
Late 20. 7. 31

THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES, JULY 19, 1931

Pick And Levitsky In Court
On Arms Dealing Charge

Pick Creates Sensation By Stating Arms Contract
Had Been Shown To Finance Minister And
Superintendent Of Customs

“I was only a small man in this business. I had to look after the shipment only, but had no word in the contract” declared Levitsky in the Shanghai Special District Court yesterday when charged on remand with Eugene Pick for posing as representatives of the National Government in an arms’ deal involving more than $1,000,-000. After several witnesses were called the case was adjourned one week.

While admitting that he knew Mr. R. K. Raphael, the complainant, very well, Pick denied that he was connected with Mr. Raphael in business. Questioned by Levitsky’s counsel, Mr. Franklin Chiu, Pick declared: “I know Raphael and his organization because they had sent ammunition up the Yangtze to communists. I know Raphael also because I had information before about him.”

Mr. Edward Carroll, a partner of P. Heath and Company who was previously stated to have been in Mr. Raphael’s office and overheard certain negotiations in connection with the deal, said he met Levitsky for the first time on May 24, when Levitsky was introduced to him by Mr. Raphael as Major Levitz, a representative of the purchasing department of the Nanking Government, negotiating for the purchase of arms. Altogether witness said, he saw Levitsky four times.

Pick Examined

Pick was then questioned by Judge Hyui as to who had witnessed the signatures in a contract relating to the arms when some difficulty arose regarding the interpretation of the question to accused. Turning to the interpreter Pick said: “You no quite understand English. You translate proper. This is not what the judge is saying.”

Cross-examined by his counsel, Mr. Paul Premet, Pick went on to say that he was told by Levitsky that when the contract was signed there were present General Chang Fah-ying, the latter’s secretary and Messrs. Raphael and Carroll. The contract was later sent to Mr. Nicholas Hsu at the General Hospital for his signature.

In reply to the judge, Levitsky said that Chang. Fah-ying was introduced to him as a general. The wording “Guaranteed by” in the contract he said, was written in Mr. Raphael’s office.

Levitsky went on to say that there were two copies of the contract and that Chang Fah-ying would not sign them unless there were two guarantors. Carroll he said, agreed to sign and Mr. Nicholas Hsu was also got to sign. Asked what the responsibilities of the guarantors were, Levitsky replied: “That is their business not mine.” In reply to further questions he said that the chop of Chang Fah-ying was placed on both copies of the contract.

Signing Of Contract

Mr. Paul Y. Ru who conducted the prosecution with Mr. R. T. Bryan Jr. Municipal Advocate then took up the examination of Levitsky who said that on the day the contract was signed he went alone to Mr. Raphael’s office. A few minutes after his arrival Messrs. Raphael and Carroll appeared and later Chang Fah-ying came.

Nicholas Hsu he said, was not present.

Continuing Levitsky said Chang Fah Ying signed the contract before it was taken to Nicholas Hsu. When he arrived in Mr. Raphael’s office witness said, the two copies of the contract already were typed out.

Mr. Ru then informed the Court that two alleged copies of the contract were produced at the last hearing when it was noticed that the wording “Guaranteed by.” appeared only in one copy. Mr. Bryan then attached some importance to this and asked that an expert be allowed to examine the two copies.

Photographic Enlargment

Detective Sub-Inspector Read of the Finger Print Bureau of the Shanghai Municipal Police who examined the copies of the contract was then called. He was of opinion that the words “Guaranteed by” and “Witness” to “Guaranteed by” were added after the contract had been typed. Witness explained that he thought those words were included after the contract had been re-set in the typewriter. Witness then gave various reasons to show why he arrived at this conclusion, and produced photographic enlargements of the documents.

Questioned by the judge Levitsky could not say whether the words “Guaranteed by” were typed on the same typewriter used for typing the contract.

Pick’s Statement

Interrogated about the documents Pick created a mild sensation in Court by declaring that he had shown the papers to Mr. T. V. Soong, Finance Minister of the National Government, and two days later had handed them to the Superintendent of Customs, as Mr. Soorg had to leave town. Pick went on to say that he handed the documents personally to the superintendent at 97 Route Ferguson. He went on to say that he was told by Levitsky that Nicholas Hsu did not want to sign the contract, but was given $20,000 by Messrs. Carroll and Raphael to do so.

Sub-Inspector Read was than cross-examined by Mr. Paul Premet and said he could not state whether the words “Guaranteed by” and “Witness” were typed on the same machine. Witness emphasized that he was not an expert on typography, but that his experience as a finger-print expert enabled him to find comparisons between the types on documents.

《上海星期时报》，1931年7月19日

皮克和莱维茨基因
军火交易指控出庭

皮克声称军火合同曾出示给财政部长
和税务司，引起轰动

“我在这笔生意中只是个小角色。我只负责照料货物运输，对合同没有发言权，”莱维茨基昨日在上海特区法院受审时宣称。他与尤金·皮克（Eugene Pick）一同被控在一笔涉及超过100万美元的军火交易中冒充国民政府代表。在传唤了几名证人后，案件休庭一周。

皮克虽然承认非常熟悉控告人 R. K. 拉斐尔先生，但否认在业务上与拉斐尔先生有关联。在莱维茨基的辩护律师富兰克林·邱（Franklin Chiu，音译）先生的讯问下，皮克宣称：“我认识拉斐尔及其组织，因为他们曾沿长江向共产党运送弹药。我也因为之前就掌握关于他的情报而认识拉斐尔。”

爱德华·卡罗尔（Edward Carroll）先生是 P. Heath 公司的合伙人，此前据称曾在拉斐尔先生的办公室，并窃听到与该交易有关的某些谈判。他说，他于5月24日首次见到莱维茨基，当时拉斐尔先生将他介绍为莱维茨少校（Major Levitz），称其是南京政府采购部的代表，正在洽谈军火采购事宜。证人表示，他总共见过莱维茨基四次。

讯问皮克

随后，惠伊法官就军火合同中见证签名的证人是谁一事讯问皮克，但在向被告解释问题时出现了一些困难。皮克转向翻译说道：“你不太懂英语。你要准确翻译。这不是法官所说的意思。”

在他的辩护律师保罗·普雷梅特（Paul Premet，音译）先生的交叉讯问下，皮克继续说道，莱维茨基告诉他，签署合同时，张发英将军、张的秘书以及拉斐尔先生和卡罗尔先生在场。合同后来被送到广慈医院（General Hospital）交给许尼古拉斯（Nicholas Hsu，音译）先生签名。

在回答法官时，莱维茨基表示，张发英是以将军的身份被介绍给他的。他说，合同中的“由……担保”（Guaranteed by）字样是在拉斐尔先生的办公室里写上去的。

莱维茨基接着说，合同有两份副本，除非有两名担保人，否则张发英不会签字。他说，卡罗尔同意签字，许尼古拉斯也被找来签字。当被问及担保人的责任是什么时，莱维茨基回答：“那是他们的事，不是我的事。”在回答进一步的问题时，他说张发英的印章盖在了两份合同副本上。

签署合同

随后，与市政检察官小 R. T. 布莱恩（R. T. Bryan Jr.）先生共同提起公诉的保罗·Y·鲁先生开始讯问莱维茨基。莱维茨基说，在签署合同的那天，他独自去了拉斐尔先生的办公室。他到达几分钟后，拉斐尔先生和卡罗尔先生出现，随后张发英也来了。

他说，许尼古拉斯不在场。

莱维茨基继续说，张发英在合同被带给许尼古拉斯之前就在合同上签了字。证人说，当他到达拉斐尔先生的办公室时，两份合同副本已经打印好了。

鲁先生随即告知法庭，在上次听证会上出示了两份所谓的合同副本，当时人们注意到“由……担保”（Guaranteed by）的字样只出现在其中一份副本上。布莱恩先生对此颇为重视，并要求允许专家检查这两份副本。

照片放大

随后传唤了上海公共租界警务处指纹局的副巡官里德（Read），他检查了合同副本。他认为，“由……担保”（Guaranteed by）字样以及其后的“见证人”（Witness）字样是在合同打印完成后添加的。证人解释说，他认为这些字样是在合同重新放入打字机排版后加入的。证人随后给出了各种理由来说明他得出这一结论的原因，并出示了文件的照片放大件。

在法官的讯问下，莱维茨基无法说明“由……担保”字样是否与打印合同的同一台打字机打出的。

皮克的陈述

在被问及文件时，皮克在法庭上引起了一阵轻微的轰动，他宣称他曾将这些文件出示给国民政府财政部长宋子文（T. V. Soong）先生，两天后又将其交给了税务司，因为宋先生要离开上海。皮克继续说，他在弗格森路（Route Ferguson）97号亲自将文件交给了税务司。他接着说，莱维茨基告诉他，许尼古拉斯不想在合同上签字，但卡罗尔先生和拉斐尔先生给了他2万美元让他签字。

随后，保罗·普雷梅特先生对副巡官里德进行了交叉讯问，里德表示他无法断定“由……担保”和“见证人”字样是否由同一台机器打出。证人强调他不是字体排印专家，但他作为指纹专家的经验使他能够对比文件上的字体类型。

（批注：注册员，请于1931年7月19日归档。）

皮克与列维茨基被控
冒充身份

警方指控被告在与国民政府洽谈军火采购时

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Wednesday, June 17, 1931

Pick, Levitsky
Held In Alleged
$1,800,000 Deal

R. K. Raphael Charges
They Posed As Canton
Military Advisors

CONTRACTS SIGNED
TO PURCHASE ARMS

Chinese Said To Have
Styled Self Brother
Of Chang Fah-kwei

Eugene Pick, Latvian, and Maurice Levitsky, Russian, central figures in the sensational "Pick case" of 1929, were brought before Judge Hyul in the Special District Court this morning and remanded for two weeks in connection with startling alleged deal involving $1,800,000 worth of arms and ammunition.

The complainant was Mr. R. K. Raphael, of 2 Canton Road, exporter and importer. Pick and Levitsky were arrested yesterday afternoon by detectives from Central Police Station.

Posed As Advisors
In court this morning Mr. Raphael stated that the two men came to his concern and represented themselves as German military advisors to the National Government. After a number of conversations, he said, contracts were signed for a supply of arms and ammunition totalling $1,800,000, to be delivered to Canton or any other port designated by the accused.

The two, according to Mr. Raphael, were accompanied by a man whose name was given as Chang Fah-ying, who claimed to be a brother of General Chang Fah-kwei.

Consulted Lawyers
The complainant asserted that he suspected the aims ordered by Pick and Levitsky were for the Canton Government and consulted his lawyers, who advised him to be careful in his dealings with the men and to compel them to comply with all necessary formalities in connection with the huge purchase.

Levitsky and Pick both testified that the former, aware of the alleged activities of Mr. Raphael in supplying arms to the Canton Government, secured work with the firm and obtained documents disclosing the alleged deals for arms with Canton.

Claims To Be Secret Agent
Levitsky, according to the statements of the men, gave the documents to Pick, who claims that he sent them to the Nanking Intelligence Bureau five days ago. Pick further asserted that he is now an agent for the bureau.

Following the complaint of Mr. Raphael, police arrested Levitsky at 467 Chapoo Road, a printing establishment, where he is alleged to have "chopped" a document with a false "chop" which had been made to his order by the printing shop.

Arrested In Frenchtown
Pick was nabbed at 24 Tracey Terrace, the Settlement police first obtaining permission from the police of the French Concession. Levitsky is 33 years of age and Pick 34 years old.

Testifying this morning, Mr Raphael declared that the two men came to him under the guise of German officers. Pick, he said, posed as Captain K. Klige and Levitsky as Major Max Levist.

Questioned Pick
Questioned by the complainant concerning the contract, which called for the delivery of the arms and ammunition at Canton or any other designated port, Pick, according to Mr. Raphael, after being told that Canton is not under the control of the Nanking Government, is stated to have replied that the arms might be used in the southern city.

It was revealed that the transaction was witnessed by Mr. Edward Carroll, British merchant, and Mr. Nicholas Chu, well-known local Chinese business man.

Inquiries Made
It further was stated that the complainant, desirous of ascertaining if the accused were bona fide representatives of the Nanking Government, made inquiries of Nanking through the British consulate general. He is stated to have been told to be cautious in his dealings.

The contract was for 1,250 pistols and 6,500 rifles, the actual value being $1,773,325.

Levitsky told the court that while working for Mr Raphael he discovered that several shipments of firearms had been delivered to Canton from Dairen. He said he reported the matter to Mr. T. V. Soong.

购买军火的合同

据称有一名华人
自称是张发奎之弟

拉脱维亚人尤金·皮克和俄罗斯人莫里斯·列维茨基（Maurice Levitsky）是1929年轰动一时的“皮克案”的核心人物，今天上午他们在特区法院海厄尔（Hyul）法官面前受审，并因涉及一起惊人的涉嫌价值180万美元的军火弹药交易而被还押两周。

原告是广东路2号的进出口商R. K. 拉斐尔先生。皮克和列维茨基于昨日下午被中央捕房的侦探逮捕。

冒充顾问

拉斐尔先生今天上午在法庭上陈述称，这两人来到他的商行，自称是国民政府的德国军事顾问。他说，经过多次会谈后，双方签署了供应总值180万美元的军火弹药的合同，货物将运往广州或由被告指定的任何其他港口。

据拉斐尔先生称，这两人由一名名叫陈发英（Chang Fah-ying）的男子陪同，此人声称是张发奎将军的兄弟。

咨询律师

原告断言，他怀疑皮克和列维茨基订购的军火是为广东政府准备的，于是咨询了他的律师，律师建议他在与这些人打交道时要小心谨慎，并迫使他们遵守与这笔巨额采购有关的所有必要手续。

列维茨基和皮克均作证说，前者知晓拉斐尔先生向广东政府供应军火的所谓活动，因此在该商行谋得职位，并获取了披露与广东进行所谓军火交易的文件。

声称是秘密特工

据两人的陈述，列维茨基将这些文件交给皮克，皮克声称他五天前已将文件送往南京情报局。皮克进一步断言，他现在是该局的一名特工。

继拉斐尔先生投诉后，警方在乍浦路467号的一家印刷店逮捕了列维茨基，据称他在那里用一家印刷店按他的要求制作的假图章在一份文件上“盖印”。

在法租界被捕

皮克是在特拉西台（Tracey Terrace）24号被捕的，租界警方事先获得了法租界警方的许可。列维茨基33岁，皮克34岁。

拉斐尔先生今天上午作证时宣称，这两人伪装成德国军官来见他。他说，皮克冒充K. 克利格上尉（Captain K. Klige），列维茨基冒充马克斯·列维斯特少校（Major Max Levist）。

讯问皮克

据拉斐尔先生称，当原告就合同询问皮克时——合同规定军火弹药需交付至广州或任何其他指定港口——在被告知广州不在南京政府控制之下后，皮克据称回答说，这些军火可能会用于这座南方城市。

据悉，英国商人爱德华·卡罗尔（Edward Carroll）先生和当地知名华商朱尼古拉斯（Nicholas Chu）先生见证了这笔交易。

进行调查

另据称，原告为了查明被告是否是南京政府的 bona fide（真正）代表，通过英国总领事馆向南京方面进行了查询。据称，他得到的答复是要在交易中保持谨慎。

合同标的为1,250支手枪和6,500支步枪，实际价值为1,773,325美元。

列维茨基告诉法庭，他在为拉斐尔先生工作期间发现，有几批枪支已从大连运抵广州。他说，他将此事报告给了宋子文（T. V. Soong）先生。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, JUNE 17, 1931

PICK AND LEVITSKY
ARRESTED AGAIN

Foreign Complainants
Allege Attempted
Swindle

Detectives from Central Police Station yesterday afternoon took into custody Eugene Pick and E. Levitsky, Russians, on information laid by two foreign complainants. The accused are held in the Central Police Station pending their appearance at the Shanghai District Court this morning.

Although full details of the alleged attempted swindle, which is said to involve an amount running into six figures, have not been disclosed, it was learned last night that arms are at the bottom of the case.

It will be recalled that Pick was the leading figure in one of the most sensational cases brought before the Shanghai Provisional Court two years ago as the result of which he was sentenced to nine months' imprisonment. Levitsky was also charged on that occasion.

（批：17/6）

EUGENE PICK IN COURT
Forging of Documents on Arms Deal
Charged Against Russians

Eugene Pick and M. Levitsky, who were the leading figures in a sensational case brought before the former Shanghai Provisional Court two years ago, were the main figures in another sensation in the Shanghai Special District Court yesterday when they were charged with being suspected of disturbing the peace of China and with forging documents.

Mr. Paul Y. Ru, Assistant Municipal Advocate, who prosecuted, asked the Court to order a two weeks' remand after hearing the evidence and to issue search warrants to enable the police to search the houses of the two accused because police expected that more evidence would be obtained to support the charges against accused as a result of these searches.

Outlining the case, Mr. Ru told the Court that, about May 20 this year, the two accused visited Messrs. R. K. Raphael, a British firm, at No. 2 Canton Road, and demanded to interview the manager. The interview was granted and accused stated that they were formerly German military officers and were at present military advisers to the Chinese Government in Nanking. They said they were sent to Shanghai by the Chinese Government to purchase a large quantity of arms and ammunition and that, through the introduction of Messrs. Jebsen & Co., 7 Hankow Road, they had come to the firm to negotiate regarding the purchase of arms. Accordingly, negotiations in this connection were opened between accused and the manager of Messrs. R. K. Raphael and, during the period of negotiations accused introduced to the manager of Messrs. R. K. Raphael, who was complainant in the case, a number of Chinese, one of whom was described as Gen. Chang Fa-ying, and stated to be a younger brother of Gen. Chang Fa-kuei, commander of the Cantonese "Iron-sides."

A draft contract was concluded whereby Messrs. Raphael would supply, through accused and Gen. Chang Fa-ying, the Chinese Government with $1,770,000 worth of arms, including 1,200 pistols and 6,500 rifles. The contract stipulated that 25 per cent. of the money for the purchase of the arms should be paid in advance to the Tatung Bank in Shanghai and the remainder, after the delivery of goods. The ammunition supposed to be ordered by the Chinese Government in Nanking was to be sent to Swatow, Kuangtung, now under the control of leaders of the anti-Chiang Kai-shek movement.

On June 10, continued Mr. Ru, the draft contract was signed by the manager of Messrs. Raphael and two other witnesses. One of whom was Mr. E. Carroll, and the other, a Chinese named Chu Tsai-hsueh. There were three copies of the contract, two of which were later given to the second accused (Levitsky), who stated that he would take them to Gen. Chang Fa-ying to be examined and properly signed.

On June 15, counsel said, a Chinese named Wu Tse-ziarg, proprietor of the Mei Tai Printing Shop at No. 467 Chapoo Road, and a friend of the manager of Messrs. Raphael, came to visit the latter and reported that several days previously, a foreigner, whose description answered that of the second accused, had visited his shop and ordered a false chop of the firm. Accordingly, complainant reported the affair to the police and Det.-Inspr. Bebenin went to the printing shop to wait for the second accused's return as, according to the informer, the latter said he would come back on the following day to take the chop which had been ordered. On the following day, the second accused visited the shop and, after carefully examining the chop made by the shop, stamped this on a copy of his contract with complainant and took it away after paying $2.50. He was arrested by Det.-Inspr. Bebenin about 100 yards from the shop. Information furnished by Levitsky led to the arrest of Pick at No. 4 Astor Road. At the police station, both accused asked to be detained at the Amoy Road Gaol.

Suspicions Aroused

Det.-Inspr. Bebenin and Det.-Sgt. Harvey having corroborated, complainant stated that, when the two accused first visited his firm, they gave their names as Major Max Levitz and Captain K. Klize respectively and stated they were German military advisers to the Nanking Government. The contract entered into between him and accused provided that the arms and ammunition supposed to be ordered by the Nanking Government should be sent to Canton or any other ports in Kuangtung as accused may desire. Complainant's suspicions were aroused in view of the fact that a revolt had been declared by the Cantonese leaders, so he consulted his legal adviser concerning the matter. As a result of these consultations, he told accused that his firm would not be responsible for the non-delivery of the goods if the arms ordered by accused were detained by the Kuangtung authorities upon their arrival in the southern province. As a precautionary measure, he consulted the British Consulate, who ordered him to take the necessary precautions.

尤金·皮克出庭受审
俄国人被控伪造军火交易文件

尤金·皮克（Eugene Pick）和 M. 列维茨基（M. Levitsky）是两年前在前上海临时法院审理的一起轰动案件中的主要人物，昨日他们又成为上海特区法院另一起轰动案件的主角，被控涉嫌扰乱中国治安及伪造文件。

起诉人、市助理检察官鲁保罗先生（Mr. Paul Y. Ru）在听取证据后，请求法庭下令将案件延期两周审理，并签发搜查令，以便警方搜查两名被告的住所，因为警方预计通过这些搜查将获得更多证据，以支持对被告的指控。

鲁先生在向法庭陈述案情概要时称，今年5月20日左右，两名被告前往广东路2号的英国商行 R. K. 拉斐尔公司（Messrs. R. K. Raphael），要求会见经理。获准会见后，被告声称他们曾是德国军官，现任南京中国政府的军事顾问。他们说，受中国政府派遣来沪购买大批军火弹药，并经汉口路7号捷成洋行（Messrs. Jebsen & Co.）介绍，前来该公司洽谈军火采购事宜。因此，被告与 R. K. 拉斐尔公司经理展开了相关谈判。在谈判期间，被告向作为本案原告的 R. K. 拉斐尔公司经理介绍了几名中国人，其中一人被称为张发英将军（Gen. Chang Fa-ying），并称其为粤系“铁军”指挥官张发奎将军（Gen. Chang Fa-kuei）的弟弟。

双方达成了一份合同草案，规定拉斐尔公司将通过被告和张发英将军，向中国政府提供价值1,770,000美元的军火，包括1,200支手枪和6,500支步枪。合同规定，军火采购款的25%应预付至上海的大通银行，余款在交货后支付。据称由南京中国政府订购的弹药将被运往广东汕头，该地目前处于反蒋介石运动领导人的控制之下。

鲁先生继续说道，6月10日，拉斐尔公司经理与另外两名见证人签署了合同草案。其中一名见证人是 E. 卡罗尔先生（Mr. E. Carroll），另一名是名为朱载学（Chu Tsai-hsueh）的中国人。合同一式三份，其中两份后来交给了第二被告（列维茨基），他称将把合同带给张发英将军审阅并正式签署。

律师称，6月15日，一名名为吴子江（Wu Tse-ziarg，音译）的中国人——他是乍浦路467号美泰印刷所的店主，也是拉斐尔公司经理的朋友——前来拜访后者，并报告说几天前，一名外貌特征符合第二被告描述的外国人曾光顾他的店铺，订购了一枚该公司的假印章。因此，原告向警方报案，警探督察贝贝宁（Det.-Inspr. Bebenin）前往印刷所蹲守，等待第二被告返回，因为据线人称，后者表示次日会回来取已订购的印章。次日，第二被告来到店铺，仔细检查了店里制作的印章后，将其盖在他与原告签订的合同副本上，支付2.50美元后带走。他在距离店铺约100码处被警探督察贝贝宁逮捕。根据列维茨基提供的信息，警方在阿斯特路4号逮捕了皮克。在警察局，两名被告均要求被关押在爱多亚路监狱。

引起怀疑

警探督察贝贝宁和警探警长哈维（Det.-Sgt. Harvey）作证 corroborated（佐证）后，原告陈述称，当两名被告初次访问其公司时，分别自称马克斯·列维茨少校（Major Max Levitz）和 K. 克利泽上尉（Captain K. Klize），并称他们是南京政府的德国军事顾问。他与被告签订的合同规定，据称由南京政府订购的军火弹药应运往广州或广东省内被告指定的任何其他港口。鉴于粤系领导人已宣布叛乱，原告对此产生怀疑，因此就此事咨询了他的法律顾问。经过这些咨询，他告诉被告，如果被告订购的军火在抵达南方省份时被广东当局扣押，其公司将对无法交货不承担责任。作为预防措施，他咨询了英国领事馆，领事馆指示他采取必要的预防措施。
